title: Transform Utility: overloads, rvalue sinks, default args
hints: `apply(const Pose&, const Point3&)` is the workhorse. Every other function should call it rather than duplicating the rotation math.
The `const std::vector<Point3>&` overload has to allocate a new vector (call `reserve` first). The `&&` overload owns its argument, so it can transform in place and hand the same buffer back.
Inside a function, a named rvalue reference is an **lvalue**. Returning it needs `return std::move(cloud);`, or you get a copy and the data pointer changes.
Default arguments belong in the declaration only: `Pose makePose(double yaw, double tx = 0, double ty = 0, double tz = 0);`
